adjudication.rationale: In `AssignmentSource.from_dict` the code returns `None` on `TypeError`/`ValueError` (e.g., unexpected/extra keys), and callers (`sync_assignee_outbound`) treat that as “no source” (`parsed_assignment_source=None`). `IssueSyncIntegration.should_sync` only blocks cycles when a non-`None` `sync_source` matches `self.org_integration.integration_id`; with `None` the guard is bypassed and syncing proceeds. The diff shows no logging/metrics on parse failure, so malformed/drifted payloads would silently disable the cycle-prevention logic.

adjudication.rationale: The new cycle-prevention guard in `IssueSyncIntegration.should_sync` returns `False` when `sync_source.integration_id == self.org_integration.integration_id` (issues.py). Since outbound assignee sync (`sync_group_assignee_outbound` -> `sync_assignee_outbound` task) iterates over *all* `external_issue_id`s linked to the group and passes along only an `AssignmentSource` derived from the inbound integration (no external-issue identifier), an inbound change from one external issue will cause outbound syncing to be skipped for every other linked issue on the same integration (same `integration_id`). This matches the finding and can leave sibling issues on the same integration out of sync.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/mixins/issues.py:390 — The source only records the immediate origin, so concurrent conflicting assignments in two integrations (A sets U1 while B sets U2) can still ping-pong A->Sentry->B->Sentry->A indefinitely, because each echo carries a different value and GroupAssignee.assign's idempotence check never short-circuits it.

adjudication.rationale: The diff’s new cycle-prevention logic in `IssueSyncIntegration.should_sync(...)` only blocks outbound sync when `sync_source.integration_id == self.org_integration.integration_id` (i.e., prevents an integration from echoing its own inbound change). It intentionally still “allow[s] other integrations to propagate changes outward” (comment + logic). From the shown code paths, inbound sync tags `GroupAssignee.assign/deassign(..., assignment_source=AssignmentSource.from_integration(integration))`, and that source is propagated through `sync_group_assignee_outbound` into the Celery task, which then calls `installation.should_sync(..., parsed_assignment_source)`. Nothing in the diff establishes any stronger de-duplication/correlation beyond the immediate source integration id, so the finding’s concern about A↔B oscillation under conflicting updates is a plausible architectural edge case. However, whether it truly “can ... indefinitely” depends on inbound webhook/task behavior not shown in this diff, so it’s not a directly verifiable defect introduced here.

However, within this diff, only assignee outbound wiring actually parses/forwards a source (`sync_assignee_outbound` parses `assignment_source_dict` and calls `installation.should_sync("outbound_assignee", parsed_assignment_source)`). There are no corresponding changes shown for status sync callers (no calls to `should_sync("outbound_status", ...)` or similar passing a source), so the new cycle-prevention mechanism is not demonstrably applied to status sync by this PR. This is an incompleteness/coverage concern rather than a concrete broken behavior introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is evaluated once at import/class definition time, causing all `AssignmentSource` instances to share the same timestamp, and suggests using `field(default_factory=timezone.now)`. This is the same underlying issue as the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/utils/sync.py:141 — to_dict()` uses `asdict`, which puts a raw `datetime` into the celery task kwargs; that is not JSON-serializable, and if a JSON serializer is used it either fails or comes back as a str, and `from_dict` then accepts it without type coercion.

adjudication.rationale: `AssignmentSource.to_dict()` returns `asdict(self)`, which includes the `queued` field as a raw `datetime` (see new `AssignmentSource` dataclass). That dict is passed directly into `sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async(kwargs={... "assignment_source_dict": assignment_source.to_dict() ...})` in `src/sentry/integrations/utils/sync.py`. Celery task kwargs are commonly JSON-serialized; a bare `datetime` is not JSON-serializable, so enqueueing can fail or be coerced unexpectedly. Additionally, `from_dict` blindly does `cls(**input_dict)` with no type coercion, so a stringified `queued` would be accepted into a `datetime`-typed field without validation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py:31 — from_dict` swallows TypeError/ValueError and returns None, so a malformed or version-skewed payload (for example an extra key added later) silently disables cycle prevention and syncs back to the originating integration.

adjudication.rationale: In this diff, cycle prevention relies on a non-None `AssignmentSource` reaching `IssueSyncIntegration.should_sync(...)`, which blocks when `sync_source.integration_id == self.org_integration.integration_id`. However `AssignmentSource.from_dict` returns `None` on `TypeError`/`ValueError` (e.g., an unexpected extra key causes `cls(**input_dict)` to raise `TypeError`), and `sync_assignee_outbound` then calls `installation.should_sync("outbound_assignee", parsed_assignment_source)` with `parsed_assignment_source=None`. That bypasses the new same-integration guard and can allow outbound syncing back to the originating integration in the presence of malformed/version-skewed task payloads.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/mixins/issues.py:411 — sync_status_outbound` gains an `assignment_source` param, but nothing populates it: the inbound status sync path does not create or propagate a source, and `should_sync("outbound_status")` is never given one, so status sync cycles are not prevented.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly wires `AssignmentSource` through the assignee outbound path (task parses `assignment_source_dict`, `installation.should_sync("outbound_assignee", parsed_assignment_source)`, and forwards it to `sync_assignee_outbound`). For status, the diff only changes the abstract `sync_status_outbound` signature to accept `assignment_source`, but shows no analogous propagation/cycle-prevention logic for status (no task/util changes, and no `should_sync(..., sync_source=...)` callsite for status in the provided diff). From what’s shown, the new param is currently unused/unpopulated, so cycle prevention for status is not implemented here (though whether it exists elsewhere can’t be verified from this diff alone).

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/mixins/issues.py:390 — The cycle check matches on `integration_id` only, so an inbound assignment from external issue A also suppresses outbound sync to a different external issue B linked on the same integration, leaving B's assignee stale.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a cycle-prevention check in `IssueSyncIntegration.should_sync` that suppresses outbound sync whenever `sync_source.integration_id == self.org_integration.integration_id`, regardless of which external issue triggered the inbound change. Given `sync_group_assignee_outbound` iterates over *all* `external_issue_ids` for the group and passes the same `assignment_source`, this will indeed block outbound updates to other linked external issues on the same integration. However, the comment explicitly states the intent is to block sync back to the same integration to prevent cycles; whether cross-issue propagation within the same integration is required cannot be verified from the diff alone, so it’s better framed as a scope/edge-case concern rather than a definite defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/mixins/issues.py:416 — assignment_source` is added to the abstract `sync_status_outbound` (no caller passes it, and status sync has nothing to do with assignment), while `sync_assignee_outbound` (line 397), which actually receives it, only gets it through `**kwargs`, so the param sits on the wrong method.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `assignment_source` being propagated specifically through the assignee outbound path: `GroupAssignee.objects.assign/deassign(...assignment_source=...)` -> `sync_group_assignee_outbound(...assignment_source=...)` -> celery task kwarg `assignment_source_dict` -> parsed `AssignmentSource` -> `installation.should_sync("outbound_assignee", parsed_assignment_source)` and then passed into `installation.sync_assignee_outbound(..., assignment_source=parsed_assignment_source)`. So it is not “on the wrong method” nor only arriving via `**kwargs` in the call shown. Separately, `sync_status_outbound` gaining an `assignment_source` parameter is visible, but the claim that “no caller passes it” or that it’s definitively wrong cannot be verified from this diff alone (no status-sync call sites are shown).

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/models/groupassignee.py:15 — Core model module now imports `sentry.integrations.services.assignment_source` at runtime even though the file already defers integration imports (`sync_group_assignee_outbound`) inside methods; it is only used in annotations, so it belongs under `TYPE_CHECKING` to avoid a models->integrations layering leak and circular-import risk.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new top-level runtime import in a core model module: `src/sentry/models/groupassignee.py` now imports `AssignmentSource` from `sentry.integrations.services.assignment_source`. That creates a direct models -> integrations dependency where the file previously deferred integration-related imports inside methods (`from sentry.integrations.utils import sync_group_assignee_outbound`), so the layering/circular-import risk concern is grounded in the diff. However, the claim that it is "only used in annotations, so it belongs under TYPE_CHECKING" is not fully verifiable as a safe change from the diff alone because `groupassignee.py` does not show `from __future__ import annotations`, so removing the runtime import without also stringifying/postponing annotations could break evaluation of annotations at function definition time. Thus the issue is architectural rather than a confirmed functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py:18 — queued` is never read anywhere, and its default `timezone.now()` is computed once at import time, so every instance gets the same stale timestamp; this is a dead, misleading field.

adjudication.rationale: In `AssignmentSource`, the dataclass field `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` evaluates `timezone.now()` at class definition/import time, so all instances created without an explicit `queued` will share the same timestamp. This is a real correctness bug; it should use `field(default_factory=timezone.now)` instead. The claim that it’s “never read anywhere” isn’t strictly provable from the diff, but the stale default timestamp behavior is.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/mixins/issues.py:382 — should_sync` is a generic gate for every sync attribute (inbound/outbound status/assignee/comments) but its new param is typed `AssignmentSource` and named `sync_source`, while every other layer calls it `assignment_source`, so the name and the scope don't match.

Callers pass the `AssignmentSource` positionally (e.g. `installation.should_sync("outbound_assignee", parsed_assignment_source)`), so the different naming (`sync_source` vs `assignment_source`) does not cause any behavioral defect. adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/mixins/issues.py:66 — Base `IssueBasicIntegration.should_sync` accepts `sync_source` but ignores it and always returns False, an unused parameter that widens the base-class contract with no need.

That parameter is not “widening the contract with no need”: new call sites pass a second argument (e.g. `installation.should_sync("outbound_assignee", parsed_assignment_source)` in `sync_assignee_outbound.py`), so the base signature must accept it to avoid `TypeError` for integrations that inherit the base implementation. adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py:22 — from_integration` is a classmethod but constructs `AssignmentSource(...)` directly instead of `cls(...)`, which is inconsistent with `from_dict` and breaks for subclasses.

This is a real inconsistency in the diff and would prevent subclasses from getting an instance of the subclass when calling `from_integration`, but the diff does not show any current subclass usage, so it’s a maintainability/design issue rather than a present functional bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py:19 — queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is evaluated once at import time, so every AssignmentSource in a worker process carries the same stale process-start timestamp instead of the actual enqueue time.

adjudication.rationale: In `AssignmentSource` the dataclass field `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` uses a callable evaluated at class definition/import time, not at instance creation. This means all `AssignmentSource()` instances created in the same worker process will share the same `queued` timestamp (process-start time), rather than reflecting when each instance was created/enqueued. The diff shows this exact pattern and no `default_factory=timezone.now` is used.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py:31 — from_dict swallows ValueError/TypeError and returns None with no logging or metric, so a malformed/incompatible payload silently disables cycle protection and the task syncs back to the originating integration.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `AssignmentSource.from_dict` (new file) catches `ValueError`/`TypeError` and returns `None` with no logging/metrics, and `sync_assignee_outbound` then passes `None` into `installation.should_sync(...)`. In `IssueSyncIntegration.should_sync`, the cycle-prevention check only runs when `sync_source` is truthy (`if sync_source and ...`), so an invalid/missing payload would indeed bypass that protection. However, the diff also shows all internal call sites serialize via `assignment_source.to_dict()` (in `sync_group_assignee_outbound`) and inbound assignment/deassignment now provides `AssignmentSource.from_integration(integration)`, so malformed payloads aren’t demonstrated by this PR; the main actionable issue is observability/robustness for compatibility/old tasks rather than a definite, reproducible defect introduced here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/tasks/sync_assignee_outbound.py:30 — New `assignment_source_dict` kwarg is sent by producers in the same deploy that adds it to the task signature, so during a rolling deploy old workers receive an unexpected kwarg, raise TypeError, and burn through 5 retries before dropping the sync.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes the Celery task signature `sync_assignee_outbound(...)` to accept a new kwarg `assignment_source_dict` (defaulting to `None`) and also updates the producer `sync_group_assignee_outbound()` to always enqueue the task with that kwarg in `apply_async(kwargs={..., "assignment_source_dict": ...})`. In a rolling deploy, an old worker running the previous task definition (without `assignment_source_dict`) would receive this unexpected kwarg and raise `TypeError`, causing retries and potential loss of the intended sync. The diff contains no backward-compat handling (e.g., accepting `**kwargs` in the task or avoiding sending the new kwarg until all workers are updated).

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/utils/sync.py:141 — to_dict() puts a raw datetime into celery task kwargs; this relies on the pickle serializer and would fail (or become a string) under a JSON/taskworker serializer, and because apply_async runs synchronously inside assign()/deassign() a serialization error would bubble up and fail the assignment request after DB writes.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does pass `assignment_source.to_dict()` into `sync_assignee_outbound.apply_async(...)` kwargs (see `src/sentry/integrations/utils/sync.py`), and `AssignmentSource.to_dict()` uses `asdict(self)` which includes `queued: datetime` (see `src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py`). That means a raw `datetime` object is being sent through Celery task kwargs, which can be a real interoperability/robustness issue depending on the configured Celery serializer (some JSON serializers won’t accept datetimes, or may coerce them unexpectedly). However, the diff alone doesn’t show Celery’s serializer configuration or whether this will actually fail in this project, so it’s not verifiably a definite defect from the diff by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py:33 — from_dict does no type coercion, so a `queued` value round-tripped as an ISO string (JSON serializer) is stored as a str in a field typed datetime, and a string integration_id would make the cycle-check equality silently fail.

adjudication.rationale: In `AssignmentSource.from_dict`, the code blindly does `return cls(**input_dict)` with no runtime type validation/coercion. Because dataclass type hints aren’t enforced, a JSON-deserialized payload like `{"integration_id": "123", "queued": "2026-..."}` will produce an `AssignmentSource` whose `integration_id`/`queued` are `str`. That directly affects the new cycle-prevention check in `IssueSyncIntegration.should_sync`: `sync_source.integration_id == self.org_integration.integration_id` will silently fail if one side is a string, allowing outbound sync when it should be blocked. The diff adds this parsing path in `sync_assignee_outbound` (`AssignmentSource.from_dict(assignment_source_dict)`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/integrations/services/assignment_source.py:31 — Tests only check that invalid dicts return None and never round-trip to_dict() -> from_dict() through the task serializer, so the datetime serialization path that cycle protection depends on is untested.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `AssignmentSource.to_dict()` using `dataclasses.asdict`, which will include the `queued: datetime` field, and passes that dict through a task kwarg (`assignment_source_dict`) which is then parsed by `AssignmentSource.from_dict()` (only `cls(**input_dict)`; no datetime-string parsing). The added tests in `tests/sentry/integrations/services/test_assignment_source.py` do not exercise a full round-trip of `to_dict()` -> (task serialization) -> `from_dict()`, nor do they validate handling of the `queued` field at all. However, the finding’s statement that cycle protection “depends on” datetime is not supported by the diff—the cycle protection check only uses `integration_id` in `should_sync`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/sentry/models/test_groupassignee.py:180 — No test covers an assignment_source from a different integration still syncing outbound, so a regression that suppresses all sourced syncs (e.g. inverted/overbroad check in should_sync) would pass the suite.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/sentry/integrations/services/test_assignment_source.py:36 — test_to_dict asserts only `queued is not None`, which passes despite the default `timezone.now()` being evaluated once at import (assignment_source.py:18), so every instance shares a stale timestamp undetected.
